hints: Think about what lipase actually makes from lipid in milk, and how those products will affect the pH you are measuring.
Ask yourself two things: how does falling substrate affect rate over 20 minutes, and what does a build-up of acid do to an enzyme kept at constant temperature?
walkthrough:
**Recall what lipase does**

Lipase hydrolyses triglyceride lipid into glycerol and fatty acids. Fatty acids are acidic, so as they accumulate the pH of the milk mixture will fall.

That means the pH readings are an indirect measure of product formed:
$$\text{triglyceride + water} \xrightarrow{\text{lipase}} \text{glycerol + fatty acids (acidic)}$$

**Explain the shape of the pH change**

At the start, substrate concentration is high ($10 \text{ cm}^3$ of high-fat milk), so many enzyme-substrate complexes form and product is made quickly. The pH therefore falls rapidly in the first few minutes.

As time proceeds, lipid substrate is used up, so fewer collisions occur and less new fatty acid is made per minute. The pH then changes less rapidly. This supports both statement 1 and statement 2.

**Link product to enzyme activity**

Temperature is kept constant, so slowing is not due to temperature. But the product itself lowers the pH further and further away from the optimum pH for lipase.

A pH far from the optimum disrupts bonds in the enzyme and gradually denatures more lipase molecules, which also slows the rate. This supports statement 3, so 1, 2 and 3 can all be supported.

options.A: Correct. Falling substrate slows product formation (1), giving a fast then slow pH fall (2), and accumulating fatty acid lowers pH and denatures lipase (3).
options.B: Incomplete. It correctly includes 1 and 2 but wrongly leaves out 3, which is also supported because acid product moves pH from optimum and denatures enzyme.
options.C: Incomplete. It leaves out statement 2, but the fast-then-slow fall in pH is exactly what you expect as substrate falls and enzyme denatures.
options.D: Incomplete. It leaves out statement 1, but decreasing lipid substrate is a key reason less fatty acid product is made per minute as time proceeds.
